findings.evidence: Use when a fast, cheap typed judgment beats a full reasoning pass: yes/no (noul), picking among named options (choice), a rubric score (score), or screening evidence against a criterion
findings.fix: Use when a fast, cheap typed judgment beats a full reasoning pass: a yes/no (noul), a pick among named options (choice), a rubric score (score), or screening evidence against a criterion (supported/partial/unsupported/unclear), including a second opinion or a caller script that must record each answer. Use even when the user says "quick check", "cheap second opinion" or "ask jev" without naming Laya, TypeSafe or a type. Not for building TypeSafe into an app (typesafe-ai), editing or refactoring code, commit messages, plan review, or choosing a GSD model profile.

findings.evidence: ## Shared-state spike (dated record) sits in the always-available reference next to request shapes, with no load condition
findings.fix: Move the dated shared-state spike and the 2026-10-15/2026-10-18 changelog sections into backends/ or a history file, and tell SKILL.md to read them only when checking a measured claim or a stale capability date.

findings.evidence: Callers use one entry point ... ladder (stdin {"items": [...]})
findings.fix: State one caller default: one ladder stdin object with one item when the selected backend is laya, and one batch only when the probe selected typesafe. Point the bare screen invocation, including reviewed_head, at reference.md as the non-caller path.

findings.evidence: 10 should-trigger queries all name jev, Laya, TypeSafe or the ladder; no should-trigger query omits those words
findings.fix: Add 2-3 should-trigger queries that ask only for a cheap yes/no, a pick among named options, or a rubric score, and keep the existing near-miss negatives.

findings.evidence: Screen calls: request shape in reference.md. The reference example is a bare jev_review.py invocation with two items and reviewed_head, while Callers requires the ladder subcommand and Laya forbids wrapping several items into one call.
findings.fix: In SKILL.md Call it, say callers always use ladder and put one item in the stdin object unless the probe selected a batch backend; in reference.md, label the bare invocation as the screen path and show one item for laya.

findings.evidence: laya is the System One server from the llm-env stack: a Jev checkpoint, local by default.
findings.fix: Delete the definition; start at the endpoint, consent and one-item rule.

findings.evidence: ## Callers and ## Call it are separate procedures for the same client, and neither says which one an agent follows.
findings.fix: Merge them into one procedure: probe, read the selected backend file, build one item, call ladder, then read ok / needs_fallback / consent_required_for_remote.
